text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today despite a strong two-week rally, as crude oil prices pulled back modestly from their recent highs. Brent crude dropped from the $109–$110 range earlier in the week to around $127 globally, while U.S. oil sits at $101.91—still elevated, but no longer accelerating. The stock had climbed nearly 9.5% over the past two weeks on the back of geopolitical tensions (Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, Iran's threats in the Strait of Hormuz) pushing crude higher; today's small decline reflects a pause in that momentum rather than any company-specific bad news.

Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity with solid inventory levels, so the operating environment remains favorable for a refiner. The modest pullback today looks like profit-taking after a sharp run-up, especially with oil prices still well above $100 per barrel—the underlying fundamentals that drove the two-week gain haven't reversed.
